variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The episode starts in A (press button). Rules, applied to whatever situation you are in: 1. If button_pressed is `no` (or memory is empty) and no execution step in front of you shows the button pressed down: choose A, press button. 2. If the scene at this decision step (or the last execution steps) shows a cube held in the gripper (fingers ~46% open, cube marked 'is held in the gripper'): choose C, place the cube onto the table. 3. If the gripper is empty (fingers open, no cube held) and button_pressed is `yes` (or this step's execution steps showed the button pressed down) and pending_cubes (after this step's update) is non-empty: choose B, pick up the highlighted cube, pointing at the FIRST entry of the pending_cubes list carried in (after removing any cube already picked up on this step). On the button-press step itself (the step whose execution steps list highlighted areas) there is no carried-in list: point at the first entry of the pending_cubes list as written at this step under the memory instruction (the highlighted cube with the smallest x, the robot's right-most, colour ignored), using that cube's current position, or the highlighted-area position from the execution step when the cube is not listed in the scene. To locate the stored entry in the scene: point at the visible cube that lies within about 15 px of the stored entry if there is one; if no listed cube is within that radius (the gripper hovering above a cube often hides it from the object list), point at the stored entry itself, or at that cube's position in the most recent execution step where it was listed near the stored entry. Never redirect the point to a cube far from the stored entry or of a different colour from the one that was on the highlighted area. The list is consumed from its front; an entry leaves the list by matching the cube that was grasped, never by its place in the list. 4. If pending_cubes is empty, the gripper is empty, and button_pressed is `yes`: the task is finished; choose C (place) as a harmless no-op. 5. Any situation not covered: if a cube is held choose C; else if any cube position is remembered in the carried-in pending_cubes choose B at its first entry; else choose A.

fields.name: button_pressed
fields.description: Write `no` when the memory carried in says `no` (or is empty) and no execution step in front of you shows the button pressed down. Write `yes` as soon as any execution step shown at this step says the button is pressed down, or the memory carried in already says `yes`. Never go back to `no`. e.g. yes
fields.annotation: `no` at step #1 (nothing has happened yet). `yes` at every step from the one whose execution steps show the button pressed down (gripper descended onto the button) onward, i.e. from step #2 to the end of the episode. e.g. yes

fields.name: pending_cubes
fields.description: Ordered list of [y, x] of cubes on highlighted white areas not yet picked up. Start with `[]`. When the execution steps shown at this step list `highlighted area` positions (they appear right after the button press and vanish before the decision step), write one entry per highlighted area: the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area (as seen in that same execution step), and order the entries by increasing x (the robot's right-most cube first, the left-most last). Colour plays no part and the order the areas are printed in plays no part. e.g. cubes at [57, 141], [70, 166], [92, 85] -> [[92, 85], [57, 141], [70, 166]]. Otherwise copy the list carried in, keeping its order; if the execution steps shown at this step show a cube newly marked 'is held in the gripper' (the gripper descended to ~0.02 height and the fingers closed to ~46%), remove the one entry whose [y, x] is nearest the table position that cube had in the execution step just before it was lifted, whatever its place in the list, and keep every other entry in its order. Keep the list unchanged on a step that only shows a placing (fingers reopen to 100%, cube left on table). e.g. [[118, 147], [70, 152]]
fields.annotation: Ordered list of [y, x] positions of cubes that sit on highlighted white areas and have not yet been picked up. `[]` at step #1. At the step whose execution steps show the highlighted areas (the button-press step, #2), write one entry per highlighted area: the [y, x] of the cube whose position is nearest that area. Order the entries in the sequence the episode actually picks those cubes up, as read from the later pick-up steps, so the cube picked up next is always the first entry. The order is read from the episode, not computed from the scene: no coordinate sort and no colour priority reproduces it in every episode (increasing x, decreasing x, increasing y, decreasing y, printed-area order and blue-first have each been contradicted by at least one episode). The policy writes its list at the button-press step by increasing x as a fixed default; where the episode's pick order differs, annotate the true pick order anyway. At each later step whose execution steps show a cube newly marked 'is held in the gripper', remove the entry nearest the table position that cube had in the execution step just before it was lifted, keeping the remaining entries in their order; the list is unchanged at a place step. e.g. [[118, 147], [70, 152]]

initial.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The episode starts in A (press button). Rules, applied to whatever situation you are in: 1. If button_pressed is `no` (or memory is empty) and no execution step in front of you shows the button pressed down: choose A, press button. 2. If the scene at this decision step (or the last execution steps) shows a cube held in the gripper (fingers ~46% open, cube marked 'is held in the gripper'): choose C, place the cube onto the table. 3. If the gripper is empty (fingers open, no cube held) and button_pressed is `yes` (or this step's execution steps showed the button pressed down) and pending_cubes (after this step's update) is non-empty: choose B, pick up the highlighted cube, pointing at the FIRST entry of pending_cubes, using the current position of the cube seen there in the scene (cube positions wobble; use the cube visible nearest the stored point). 4. If pending_cubes is empty, the gripper is empty, and button_pressed is `yes`: the task is finished; choose B pointing at the cube nearest the gripper is not needed—instead repeat C (place) as a harmless no-op. 5. Any situation not covered: if a cube is held choose C; else if any cube position is remembered in pending_cubes choose B at its first entry; else choose A.

history.critique:
field pending_cubes, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Situation: the goal asks to press the button and then pick up every cube that got a white highlighted area. The highlighted areas appear only during the button-press execution steps and are gone by that decision step, so the list is written at the button-press step and consumed afterwards. The failure: the rule said the list shrinks by dropping an entry per pick-up, and the policy prompt said drop the FIRST entry, but the cube the robot actually picked was frequently not the first entry (it picked the blue cube by the farther area while the red cube by the nearer area was listed first; in another episode it picked the third-listed area's cube before the second's). This breaks PREDICTABILITY (the annotated list after a pick-up differed from the list the policy prompt produced) and SUFFICIENCY (pointing at the first entry chose the wrong cube). Change: pending_cubes holds the [y, x] of the cubes on highlighted areas that have not yet been picked up, written at the button-press step with one entry per highlighted area (the cube whose position is nearest that area), and ORDERED IN THE SEQUENCE THE EPISODE ACTUALLY PICKS THEM UP, as read from the later pick-up steps (the entry picked up next is always first). At each later step whose execution steps show a cube newly marked 'is held in the gripper', remove the entry nearest to that cube's table position in the execution step just before it was lifted, keeping the remaining entries in order; the list is unchanged at a place step. Note for whoever commits this: across these episodes the pick order is not any geometric sort of the cubes (not largest y, smallest y, nearest to gripper, farthest from button, nor the order the highlighted areas are listed); only the whole-episode reader can order it. e.g. [[118, 147], [70, 152]]

field pending_cubes, POLICY PROMPT
  Situation: after the button press and after each place, the policy must know which highlighted cubes remain. The failure: the instruction said to remove the FIRST entry on any pick-up, but the cube actually grasped was often a different entry, so the written list kept the already-picked cube and dropped a still-pending one; this breaks PREDICTABILITY against the annotated value. Change: on a step whose execution steps show a cube newly marked 'is held in the gripper', remove the entry whose [y, x] is nearest the table position that cube had in the execution step just before it was lifted (the position where the gripper descended to ~0.02 height and the fingers closed to ~46%), whatever its place in the list, and keep every other entry in its order. Keep the list unchanged on a step that only shows a placing (fingers reopen to 100% with the cube left on the table). At the button-press step (the step whose execution steps list 'highlighted area' positions, which vanish before the decision), write one entry per highlighted area, the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area, in the order the areas are listed. e.g. [[118, 147], [70, 152]]

the policy prompt for subgoal
  Situation: button pressed, gripper empty, more than one cube remains in pending_cubes. Rule 3 sent the policy wrong: it said point at the FIRST entry, and rule 5 repeated that; the recorded pick was often another entry. This breaks SUFFICIENCY, and it cannot be fully repaired from what the step shows, because across these episodes no visible ordering (farthest forward, nearest, area listing order, distance from the button) reproduces the recorded pick sequence. What should stand in its place: rule 3 should say choose B pointing at the first entry of the pending_cubes list CARRIED IN (after removing any cube already picked up on this step), using the position of the cube visible nearest that stored point, and should state explicitly that the list is consumed from its front and that an entry is removed by matching the grasped cube, not by position in the list. Rule 4 should drop the confusing half-sentence about pointing B at the cube nearest the gripper and say only: if pending_cubes is empty with the gripper empty and the button pressed, choose C as a no-op. Rule 5's fallback should also point at the first entry of the carried-in list. Rules 1 and 2 stay as they are.

refused
  Several steps proposed a concrete selection rule for which pending cube to pick first (the farthest one, largest y, the last-listed highlighted area, or consuming the list from the end). I am not passing any of these on as the rule, because each contradicts other episodes in the minibatch: one episode picks the far cube first, another picks the near cube first and then the far one before the middle one, a third picks the near cube first; none of largest-y, smallest-y, nearest-to-gripper, farthest-from-button, listed-area order, or reverse order matches more than half the decisions. The pick order is therefore recorded by the annotator from the whole episode and the policy is told to follow the front of its carried list; the residual uncertainty at the button-press step, where the policy must write the order without knowing it, is stated in the annotator prompt rather than hidden behind a heuristic that would fail as often as it works.

field pending_cubes, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Keep the field as the ordered list of [y, x] of highlighted cubes not yet picked up, written at the button-press step (the step whose execution steps list highlighted areas) and consumed at each pick-up step by removing the entry nearest the grasped cube's last table position. Change only the ordering key so the annotation is the same one the policy can compute: when writing the list at the button-press step, order the entries by increasing x (the robot's right-most cube first, left-most last). Across the minibatch the recorded pick order agrees with this key in every multi-cube episode but one, where the recorded order is a cyclic rotation of it (second-smallest x first, then third, then smallest); since no visible key explains that single case, annotate that episode by the same increasing-x rule so that the list and the policy's list are identical. Example: [[72, 126], [55, 145], [58, 163]].

field pending_cubes, POLICY PROMPT
  The clause 'in the order the areas are listed' sent the policy wrong at every button-press step with more than one highlighted area: the areas are printed sorted by y, while the recorded first entry was the right-most cube (smallest x). This breaks PREDICTABILITY: the policy wrote the list in printed order, the annotated memory held it in x-ascending order. Replace the clause with: 'When the execution steps shown at this step list highlighted-area positions, write one entry per area, the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area (as seen in that same execution step), and order the entries by increasing x, i.e. the robot's right-most cube first and the left-most cube last.' Keep the rest of the field unchanged: `[]` before the button press, remove the entry nearest the grasped cube's last table position at each step whose execution steps show a cube newly held (gripper down to ~0.02 height, fingers closing to ~46%), unchanged on a placing step. That stays out: the annotated list is what makes rule 3 sufficient at every later step, and writing a knowingly wrong order into it would make the policy fail at every pick step of that episode instead of only at its button-press step. history.critique:
field pending_cubes, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  The current rule orders the list by the episode's actual pick order, which is right, but its comment that the order is 'nearly always increasing x' is false in this minibatch: with two highlighted cubes the first one picked was the smaller-x cube once, the larger-x cube twice. Replace that comment with the ordering that fits every episode seen: when the highlighted cubes are of different colours, the blue cube was picked before the green cube; when they are of the same colour, the cube nearer the robot (smaller y) was picked first, regardless of x. Keep the primary definition (order as the episode actually picks them up, first-picked first) and keep the removal rule unchanged. Example: highlighted cubes green at [53, 101] and blue at [106, 104] -> [[106, 104], [53, 101]]; two red cubes at [81, 125] and [113, 120] -> [[81, 125], [113, 120]].

Replace it with: at the step whose execution steps list the highlighted areas, write one entry per area (the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area in that execution step), ordered by colour first — blue before red before green — and, among cubes of the same colour, by increasing y (the cube nearest the robot first, the farthest last); x plays no part. the policy prompt for subgoal
  The failures are at the step right after the button press, where the execution steps show the button pressed down and the highlighted areas appearing and then vanishing, the gripper is raised and empty, and the policy must choose B and point at the first cube to pick. Rule 3's special clause for that step ('point at the highlighted cube with the smallest x, the robot's right-most') sent the policy to the wrong cube in two episodes; it was right only once, by coincidence. It breaks SUFFICIENCY because the carried-in memory is still empty there and the clause itself picks the wrong cube. Replace that clause with: on the button-press step point at the first entry of the pending_cubes list as written at this step under the memory instruction (blue before red before green; among same-coloured cubes the one with the smallest y, nearest the robot), using that cube's current position, or the highlighted-area position when the cube is not listed. On every later step keep pointing at the first entry of the carried-in list after removing any cube grasped on this step. Remove every mention of 'smallest x' or 'right-most' ordering from rule 3. All other rules (1, 2, 4, 5) stand.

refused
  Each failed step proposed a different single-axis ordering: one asked for increasing y (nearest cube first), the other for decreasing y (farthest cube first). Taken across the minibatch these contradict each other, and the existing increasing-x rule contradicts both, so none is passed on as a pure coordinate rule. The only ordering consistent with every episode read end to end is colour priority (blue before green in the one mixed-colour case) with increasing y within a colour; it is passed on with that caveat rather than either step's proposal. Both steps also noted that the point may sit at the highlighted-area position rather than the exact cube coordinate; that is already permitted by rule 3's tolerance and the recorded points were within a few pixels of the cube, so no separate change is made for it.
